sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-HA immunostaining on intact blocked/fixed cells (L2). Channel electrophysiological function not explicitly reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: L1 names the junction explicitly as between position 50 (Ala) and position 51 (Arg); Python lookup confirms seq[49]='A' and seq[50]='R', both matching the paper's residue identities exactly. The site sits 21 residues from the TM1 C-boundary (residue 29) and 58 residues from the TM2 N-boundary (residue 108), satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance rule on both sides. It is 46 residues upstream of the GYG selectivity-filter motif (residues 95–97), placing it well away from the pore-forming region. L2 independently confirms that the HA tag is accessible on the extracellular surface of intact cells. Full-length human TASK-1 (KCNK3) construct with an HA epitope tag inserted between A50 and R51 in the first extracellular loop (ECL1, residues 30–107), expressed in mammalian cells. L2 confirms surface display: intact cells were blocked, fixed, and incubated with anti-HA antibody, detecting the tag on the extracellular face.

sources.claim: An HA epitope was added to the extracellular loop of TASK-1 between positions 50 (Ala) and 51 (Arg) for the extracellularly tagged TASK-1.

literature_notes: L3 and L4 describe a rat TASK-1–GFP construct cloned into pEGFP-C1, which appends GFP to the N-terminus of the insert. The KCNK3 N-terminus (residues 1–8) is intracellular per the topology landmarks; therefore the GFP moiety faces the cytoplasm and this is not an extracellular surface tag. It is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports a tag in ECL2 (residues 180–222) or at any other extracellular position.

literature_other_positions.note: Rat TASK-1 cloned into pEGFP-C1 places GFP at the N-terminus; KCNK3 residues 1–8 are intracellular, so GFP faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
